brief.text: A header is never longer than this.

content.text: The encoder fills a buffer of this size and writes only the bytes it used.

brief.text: A 1 byte header holds the length in the byte itself, so both ends of this range are the same numbers as the first byte's own range.
48 values of the first byte mean a 2 byte header, and each of them covers 256 lengths.

content.text: The 48 is worked out from the two range ends above, so it stays right if either of them changes.

brief.text: 14 values of the first byte mean a 3 byte header, and each of them covers 65,536 lengths.

content.text: Counted the same way, that gives the largest length any header can state.
Nothing is accepted or rejected against this. The assertion below uses it to check that every length the encoder writes is one a header can state.

brief.text: The largest length the encoder will write.

content.text: This is the one number here that is picked rather than worked out. The decoder accepts nothing above it, so both sides agree on the same set of lengths.

brief.text: Works out how long a header is, from its first byte.

content.text: Each overload of decodeVLLength below reads one header length, so call this first to learn which of them to call.

returns.text: How many bytes the whole header takes, counting firstByte: 1, 2 or 3.
